newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Wang to grow core services unit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Wang to grow core services unit.

text.p: Wang Laboratories Inc Chief Executive Joseph Tucci said Wednesday the $260 million cash from the sale of its software unit to Eastman Kodak Co will be used for acquisitions to strengthen its core services business.

"We'll use the cash to grow internally as well as do more acquisitions," Tucci told Reuters. "I have told our shareholders at every meeting I've had with them that I intend to grow this company rapidly."
Wang will use the cash to invest in its network and desktop integration and outsourcing areas of its service business.

Tucci said Wang plans to sell, spin off or create joint ventures out of other non-core, non-service assets. Within the next six months, some sort of deal will be done with Wang's small health care software unit, he said.
"That might be the next one," Tucci said. "We could joint-venture it, but do something where we can create value for our shareholders out of something that we've been building for awhile."
Services accounted for $256.5 million or about 70 percent of its total revenues of $363.7 million in the second quarter, announced earlier Wednesday.
Divesting from non-core units will unlock the "untapped value" of those assets and allow the investment community to put a proper valuation on Wang, Tucci said.
"This makes us now a pure services play. It will be easier for the investment community to track Wang and value Wang," he said.

Tucci said the negotiations to sell the unit, which is losing money but growing rapidly, started in September but were snagged by tax and personnel concerns. The delay in the sale impacted second quarter earnings, he added.
"The business is losing money, and obviously the shareholders get the benefit that we don't have to fund that business any more and they get $260 million," he said.
"It gives us more earnings and more cash in the coffers to grow the services business," he added.
